raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old Caucasian female with ulcerative colitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, and cirrhosis presented with fever, chills, shortness of breath, dry cough, and chest pain for five days after being started on prednisone 40 mg daily and azathioprine 50 mg daily for autoimmune hepatitis two months earlier. She was born and raised in New York state and only travelled to Vermont and Florida. During the prior two weeks, she traveled to a hunting shack in northern New York and had been there twice before becoming ill. She had no personal or family history of tuberculosis and has had several prior negative PPDs during nursing school. On presentation, she was febrile to 102 F, pulse of 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and blood pressure of 96/58 mmHg and required 2 liters oxygen to keep her saturation above 90%. Initial exam was benign with clear lungs. After blood and urine cultures were obtained, vancomycin and meropenem were started empirically. A paracentesis was not performed due to small ascitic fluid pockets. Initial chest X-ray showed trace left-sided pleural effusion without any evidence of infiltrates. Initial lab work showed ALT 62 U/L, AST 87 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 158 U/L, total bilirubin 13.2 mg/dL, INR of 2.9, WBC of 16,000/ul with 14,400/uL neutrophils, hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, and platelets of 167,000/uL. After a CT chest revealed small bilateral cavitary nodules the following day, vancomycin and meropenem were continued along with amphotericin being started with concern for a fungal infection (Figure 1).
Without clinical improvement, a CT guided biopsy of the necrotic pulmonary nodules was performed by interventional radiology three days after admission. The CT chest of the biopsy showed a new right upper lobe lesion (Figure 1) despite being on meropenem, vancomycin, and amphotericin. A bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage was performed the following day and Gram stain, fungal stain, and extensive cultures were all negative. With continued deterioration six days after the biopsy, a repeat CT chest showed increasing size and number of pulmonary nodules with ground glass opacities despite treatment with meropenem, vancomycin, and amphotericin. On day eleven of admission, cultures from the CT guided biopsy turned positive for Legionella. The antimicrobials were stopped and levofloxacin was started and continued for 3 weeks with resolution of symptoms. The culture was sent to the New York State Department of Health in Albany, NY, and identified as L. micdadei. Negative tests included normal transthoracic echo, normal head CT, and normal neck ultrasound. Five blood cultures, respiratory viral panel, urine Legionella antigen, Pneumocystis DNA PCR, Legionella culture from BAL, bacterial culture, fungal culture, Aspergillus antigen, and Histoplasma antigen were negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old Caucasian female with autoimmune hepatitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, cirrhosis, and ulcerative colitis presented with a 5-day history of fever, chills, shortness of breath, dry cough, and chest pain two months after starting prednisone and azathioprine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two months prior to admission, the patient was started on oral prednisone (40 mg daily) and azathioprine (50 mg daily) for autoimmune hepatitis. During the 2 weeks before presentation, she visited a hunting shack in northern New York twice. Five days prior to hospital admission, she developed high fever, chills, shortness of breath, dry cough, and pleuritic chest pain.
subjective.past_medical_history: Autoimmune hepatitis (started on prednisone 40 mg/day and azathioprine 50 mg/day 2 months prior); ulcerative colitis; primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC); cirrhosis. Epidemiological history: Born and raised in New York state, recent visits to a hunting shack in northern New York, prior travel limited to Vermont and Florida; several negative tuberculin PPD skin tests during nursing school; no family history of tuberculosis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, shortness of breath, dry cough, and chest pain. Home medications included prednisone 40 mg daily and azathioprine 50 mg daily.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: Temperature 102 °F, pulse 120 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, requiring 2 L/min supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 >90%. Initial chest auscultation and systemic exam were benign with clear lungs.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory tests: WBC 16,000/μL (neutrophils 14,400/μL), hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, platelets 167,000/μL, ALT 62 U/L, AST 87 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 158 U/L, total bilirubin 13.2 mg/dL, and INR 2.9. Negative microbiological screening: Five blood cultures, urine cultures, respiratory viral panel, and urinary Legionella antigen all negative. Imaging: Initial chest X-ray showed a trace left pleural effusion without focal infiltrates; transthoracic echocardiogram, head CT, and neck ultrasound were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Serial chest CT scans: Day 2 chest CT revealed small bilateral cavitary pulmonary nodules; day 4 CT (at biopsy) showed a new right upper lobe lesion; day 10 CT showed increasing size and number of cavitary pulmonary nodules with surrounding ground-glass opacities despite broad-spectrum therapy. Day 5 bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL): Negative Gram stain, fungal stain, bacterial/fungal/Legionella BAL cultures, Pneumocystis DNA PCR, Aspergillus antigen, and Histoplasma antigen. Day 4 CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of necrotic pulmonary nodules: Culture grew Legionella species on hospital day 11, definitively speciated by the New York State Department of Health (Albany, NY) as Legionella micdadei.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Cavitary necrotizing Legionella micdadei pneumonia in an immunosuppressed patient on prednisone and azathioprine for autoimmune hepatitis/PSC/cirrhosis, definitively confirmed by CT-guided lung biopsy culture and reference laboratory speciation after negative urinary Legionella antigen, negative BAL cultures, and negative Pneumocystis DNA PCR. Plan and clinical course: Initial empiric vancomycin, meropenem, and amphotericin B failed to prevent radiographic progression of cavitary nodules. On hospital day 11, upon isolation of L. micdadei from the lung biopsy culture, meropenem, vancomycin, and amphotericin B were discontinued and targeted oral/IV levofloxacin was administered for 3 weeks, resulting in complete resolution of symptoms.
